slices.focus: Contractor-backed summer boot camp runs, giving earlier visibility into incoming apprentice readiness
slices.summary: The scaled-down summer boot camp runs successfully, feeding into first-year classes and giving Derek earlier visibility into incoming apprentices. Using donated contractor materials for multiple stations, he works apprentices one-on-one and quickly identifies three distinct problem buckets: transportation/logistics barriers, basic tool unfamiliarity, and confidence issues that look like discipline problems in group settings. He designs a simple handoff sheet for instructors that tags these buckets using observable behavior language rather than labeling apprentices, protecting nervous beginners from being branded before classes start.
open_loops: Formalizing only the handoff sheet and station definition, not the whole camp
Thanking contractors specifically for enabling the material donation
Teaching one other instructor to run the basic tool station next round
Building intake notes that tag transportation, tool-readiness, and confidence buckets
Protecting pacing: long days on feet + coaching is physically demanding
decisions: Derek now oversees a contractor-backed pre-apprenticeship boot camp that feeds into the first-year classes and gives him
